name: Greenhouse pest sniffer
subtitle: a laser that smells plants under attack

effects.effect: flickering light absorbed by a gas makes it give off sound

effect: flickering light absorbed by a gas makes it give off sound
how: By the time growers see pests in a greenhouse, they have often spread through the crop and must be sprayed heavily. Leaves being chewed release a puff of cut-grass scent within minutes; a flickering infrared laser tuned to that scent makes the air in a small chamber hum whenever the scent is present, and a microphone hears it at a few parts per billion, pointing growers to the exact bay to treat.
obstacle: Making the laser sensor cheap and sturdy enough for every bay, and telling attack scent from the smell of pruning and harvest.
why: Early, targeted treatment cuts both pesticide use and crop losses.
real: Herbivore-induced green leaf volatiles are detected with e-noses, MOF sensors, portable GC and PTR-MS, but no photoacoustic GLV sensor for pest detection was found.
